title: Knee Drops as a dance step, and Gene Krupa's love of the record
summary: Zutty explains Knee Drops was a dance in which dancers dropped to their knees, and says Gene Krupa loved the tune; a fellow told him the record is in the Smithsonian.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Oh yes, I see. And now Knee Drops were from dances, that's a thing from dancing isn't it? Where they just drop on their knees.
Knee Drops, I don't know how, how they got, I guess that's what it was from. They called it Knee Drops.

You called the dance Knee Drops when you dropped to your knees and come back up again, you know. And I guess that's where Louis got the idea from. Because they really Louis' Knee Drops and that other thing. That boy told me that was in the Smithsonian Institute. Old Gene Krupa used to love that tune. Because he was living on Riverside Drive and he had that record.
When was that, do you remember?
Yes, when Mez was driving his car, you know. When Mez had the ford?
You see, he was playing at the, at the Alvin Theater.
Yes. Benny Goodman was in the band.
Well what's in the Smithsonian Institute you said?
Oh, 'Knee Drops' and something else. Because (Buddy?) told me about it.
Yes. But I don't remember ( Unintelligible ?) I heard him saying he saw it in the Smithsonian Institute.
